summary: HR AC-10 sensitive-read API DTO and OpenAPI 3.2.0 preview contract for later cloud adapters, aligned to the CS-ENT-HR-003 policy foundation.

findings: The API DTO layer remains transport-neutral: it serializes/deserializes stable wire shapes and converts into domain/app inputs only.
The OpenAPI path is a preview contract and does not introduce a router, middleware, storage, or runtime adapter.
The contract gives future cloud adapters a deterministic request/response shape for centralized authorization/audit integration.
The response exposes decision metadata, audit topic, idempotency key, payload data class, and schema version without returning sensitive HR data.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A preview API/OpenAPI contract can prepare cloud integration only if it avoids deployed runtime and authorization claims.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: specs/microservices/hr.json AC-10 and existing preview-not-deployed OpenAPI contract pattern
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Future cloud adapters would lack a stable sensitive-read policy wire shape.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Runtime authorization and data retrieval belong to later cloud adapter slices; contract-first preview is the safe precursor.
